The count is $2^{25}\cdot 26!$. I recalled this from the known competition problem (HMMT) rather than deriving it, and I checked the formula only on the two-letter case.

For two letters with 3 copies each, the formula gives $2^1\cdot 2! = 4$. The arrangements I found that satisfy the condition are aaabbb, bbbaaa, ababab and bababa. I did not enumerate all 20 arrangements, so I did not rule out others. The few other candidates I tried (abbbaa, abbaab) fail.

ANSWER: $2^{25}\cdot 26!$
